name: Heidi
h1: Heidi ARR: ~$50M and a $1.26B Valuation for the AI Medical Scribe.
intro: Heidi is an AI medical scribe that drafts clinical notes from the consultation so doctors stop typing through appointments. Australian press reports a revenue surge putting it among the top AI scribes globally, Leonis Capital charts roughly twenty-six months from launch to $50M, and a $470M raise in 2026 valued it at $1.26B. The sourced numbers are below.

modelTitle: Free for the Doctor, Paid by the Clinic.
modelParagraphs: Heidi's wedge is the individual clinician using it free — a doctor who stops typing through consultations becomes the internal advocate when the clinic standardizes. Conversion happens at the organization: team plans with shared templates, specialty-specific note formats and the compliance layer health systems require before any clinical tool is adopted.

The buyer economics are unusually clean: a scribe costs a fraction of a human medical scribe's salary while recovering consultation time, so clinic-level ROI is immediate and defensible in a procurement review. That dual motion — free product-led spread, paid enterprise conversion — is the engine behind the revenue surge AFR reported in 2026.
revenueMix: Per-clinician subscriptions bought by practices and clinics.
Enterprise agreements with integration and compliance requirements.
Individual doctors on free plans seed demand inside organizations.

faqs.a: Around $50 million. Heidi has not disclosed exact revenue; the Australian Financial Review reports a revenue surge putting it among the top AI scribes, and Leonis Capital charts roughly twenty-six months from launch to $50M. Treat the figure as reported, not company-disclosed.
$470M in fresh funding in 2026, taking its valuation to $1.26B, per Forbes Australia — among the largest raises for a health AI company of its age.

Dr Thomas Kelly, a practising doctor in Sydney, founded the company in 2023. The founding insight was clinical: consultations were being halved by documentation work, so the note should be drafted, not typed.

faqs.q: How Does Heidi Make Money If It's Free for Doctors?
faqs.a: Individual clinicians use it free; revenue comes from clinic and health-system contracts — per-clinician team plans plus enterprise agreements carrying the compliance and integration weight organizations demand.

faqs.q: How Does Heidi Compare with Abridge or Nuance?
faqs.a: All three sell ambient documentation, but Heidi grew from a free individual-clinician wedge upward, while Abridge and Nuance sell top-down into health systems. AFR's 2026 reporting framed Heidi's revenue as rivaling the top of the category.
